{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — FX Trading Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Review findings against playbook positions

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is, on the whole, acceptable: the licence is expressly non-exclusive, the fee structure is purely usage-based with volume-band discounts and no minimum commitment, there are no liquidated damages, no MFN and no non-compete binding us, and governing law and venue (New York; exclusive jurisdiction in New York City) match our preferred position.

The difficulty is that the risk-allocation articles run almost entirely one way in the Licensor's favour. Eleven findings sit at deviation or missing, several of them in playbook walk-away territory:

- **Warranty.** The Licensed Technology is provided wholly "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty or remedy.
- **Indemnification.** There is no Licensor IP indemnity at all; instead, Article XIII expressly negates Licensor liability for infringement claims, while Article XII imposes a one-way indemnity on us.
- **Limitation of liability.** Licensor's liability is capped at one half of amounts paid; our liability is uncapped, with no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnity, gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
- **Term and exit.** A 36-month initial period with a unilateral Licensor option to extend by a further seven years, no Customer termination for convenience, and automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our change of control.
- **Transition and data.** Article XXI runs one way (we ship everything back within five days); nothing requires the Licensor to return or export our trade, order and client data, or bars deletion.

On a hosted FX trading platform, the combination of no warranty, no vendor indemnity, an asymmetric liability cap, no exit right and no data-return obligation is not a risk profile we can recommend signing. Redlines have been prepared for each item, with fallbacks flagged where a landing zone exists.

---

## 2. Findings

| Sev | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us; licence is expressly non-exclusive. |
| High | LD | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation | No liquidated damages, late-payment penalty, shortfall charge or early-termination fee. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions | Restraints are internal to the licence (field of use, use restrictions); no restraint on our business. |
| Medium | GOVLAW | Compliant | General Provisions | New York law; exclusive jurisdiction in New York City; no arbitration clause. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | Fee schedule (volume bands) | No MFN or best-price obligation; "other licensees" reference runs in our favour. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions | Fees are usage-based; volume bands are discounts only, no take-or-pay or shortfall. |
| **Medium** | **TRANSITION** | **Missing** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI) | No transition assistance and no Licensor obligation to return, export or certify deletion of our data; Article XXI runs one way only. **Walk-away.** |
| **Medium** | **WARRANTY** | **Deviation** | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) | Wholly "AS IS", all warranties disclaimed, no conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy. **Walk-away.** |
| **Low** | **ASSIGN** | **Deviation** | General Provisions § (c); Art. XX(a) | Blanket bar on our assignment with no affiliate/M&A carve-out; automatic termination of Agreement and licences on our change of control. **Walk-away (two triggers).** |
| Low | AUDIT | Deviation | Fee/audit provisions | Audit mechanics are otherwise acceptable, but there is no frequency limit — unlimited audits fail the fallback. |
| **Low** | **INDEMN** | **Deviation** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XII–XIII) | No Licensor indemnity; Article XIII negates Licensor liability for IP infringement; one-way Licensee indemnity. **Walk-away.** |
| Low | INSURANCE | Missing | General Provisions | No insurance covenant anywhere; only a pass-through of insurance charges payable by us. |
| Low | IP | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. III) | One-way ownership: enhancements we commission and pay for become Licensor-owned; no reservation of rights in our data. |
| Low | LICENSE | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions | Grant limited to Licensee employees; Affiliates and contractors excluded, and licence does not survive an M&A transfer. |
| **Low** | **LOL-CAP** | **Deviation** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) | Licensor capped at one half of amounts paid; our liability uncapped; one-way consequentials exclusion; no carve-outs. **Walk-away.** |
| **Low** | **NOSOLICIT** | **Deviation** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) | One-way non-solicit for Term plus three years covering all Licensor and Affiliate personnel. **Walk-away (duration and scope).** |
| **Low** | **RENEWAL** | **Deviation** | § II / Art. IV | Unilateral Licensor option to extend the 36-month term by seven years, no Customer opt-out, no pricing cap. **Walk-away.** |
| **Low** | **T4C** | **Deviation** | § II / Art. IV | No Customer termination for convenience in a 36-month term; termination rights run to Licensor only. **Walk-away.** |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

These sit in playbook walk-away territory and, in our view, must move before signature:

1. **Warranty disclaimer (Art. VIX).** We need an express performance/conformance warranty with a repair-replace-refund remedy, carved out of the AS IS disclaimer. Preferred: professional and workmanlike services, 12-month software/Documentation conformance, compliance with laws, no malicious code. Fallback: 90-day/30-day periods.
2. **No vendor indemnity (Art. XII–XIII).** We need a Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, expressly carved out of the Article XIII exclusions so it is not illusory, and our indemnity narrowed to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of law. Fallback: usual IP exclusions with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x fees super-cap.
3. **Asymmetric liability cap (Art. XIII).** Cap must be mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with the consequentials exclusion made mutual and Excluded Claims carved out. Fallback: mutual 12-month fee cap with indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs.
4. **Change-of-control auto-termination and assignment bar (Art. XX(a); Gen. Prov. § (c)).** Delete the auto-termination (convert to a 30-day notice obligation), add affiliate/successor carve-outs, and apply a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard with a no-competitor limit on Licensor assignment.
5. **Renewal (Art. IV).** The unilateral seven-year Licensor extension option must go. Preferred: successive 12-month renewals, 30-day Licensee opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 60-day window with a 5% cap.
6. **No Customer termination for convenience (Art. IV).** Insert a Licensee convenience right on 30 days' notice with prepaid-fee refund. Fallback: 60–90 days' notice with a fee capped at three months' fees.
7. **Transition assistance and data return (Art. XXI).** Insert six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, deletion with written certification thereafter, and a bar on deletion before return is complete. Fallback: 90 days' assistance with a 30-day export.
8. **Non-solicit (Art. X(b)).** Make mutual, cut the tail from three years to twelve months, and limit to personnel directly involved in performance. The existing general-advertising carve-out is adequate and stays.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline.** All items above are drafted. Send as a single package with playbook-prefixed comments identifying the preferred position and, where noted, the fallback.
2. **Sequence the negotiation.** Treat items 1–6 as gating (warranty, indemnity, liability cap, change of control, renewal, termination for convenience). Items 7–8 and the remaining low-severity deviations can be traded in a second pass.
3. **Secondary asks to close out:**
   - **IP (Art. III):** carve out Licensee Data, assign customization deliverables to us with a licence back to embedded Licensor IP, and bar joint ownership. Licensor keeping its base platform is acceptable.
   - **Licence scope (Art. II):** extend to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with us responsible for their compliance) and permit transfer to a successor on written notice.
   - **Audit:** cap at once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site, confidential auditor, no system access. Existing notice and cost-allocation mechanics are unchanged.
   - **Insurance:** insert the coverage covenant as a new General Provisions subsection. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
4. **Confirm the commercial read.** Business team to confirm our understanding that the volume bands operate purely as discounts on trades actually executed and that the $2,500/month support fee and 33% Supplemental Payments revenue share are as modelled.
5. **Escalate if resisted.** If the Licensor declines to move on the warranty, indemnity or liability items, escalate before further drafting rounds — the residual risk on a hosted platform holding our trade and client data is outside our approved tolerance.
"}
